content.metaDescription: Bring instant calm to your hallway with this Japandi Japanese ink landscape set of 3 wall art prints — black pines, a maroon sun & a lone fisherman. Free UK shipping!
content.productDescription:
Bring a sense of real stillness into your home with this calming wall art — a set of three Japanese ink-style landscape prints that feel like a quiet breath of fresh air the moment you look at them. Each print is painted in a loose, expressive brushwork style inspired by traditional East Asian ink wash art: sweeping black and grey mountain forms rise from a crisp white ground, ancient pine trees twist dramatically against the open sky, a tiny lone fisherman drifts in his boat, a stone lantern stands quietly on a misty ridge, and at the heart of the central print glows a soft maroon-toned sun — the one warm note that ties the whole set together beautifully.

Together, the three prints tell one continuous story across your wall. The palette is wonderfully restrained — deep blacks, soft cool greys, dusty taupe-toned maroon, and lots of clean white space — which is exactly what makes them so at home in a Japandi or minimalist hallway. There is nothing fussy or loud here; just calm, considered art that quietly makes a big impression.

What's Included with Calming Wall Art Japanese Ink Landscape with Maroon Sun, Black Pine Trees & Lone Fisherman | Set of 3

  • A set of 3 individual art prints, each featuring a distinct section of the Japanese ink landscape scene
  • Printed in the UK using fade-resistant pigment inks for long-lasting colour and clarity
  • Suitable for indoor display
  • Framed and canvas-wrapped options arrive ready to hang straight out of the box — no hunting for a frame that fits, no extra hassle
  • Choose between unframed and framed options in multiple sizes and in Luster or Museum quality; also available in wrapped canvas size options

How to Style calming wall art in Your Hallway

I'd hang all three prints in a horizontal row along your hallway wall, spacing them evenly with a small gap between each — somewhere between 5 and 8 cm tends to look intentional without feeling cramped. Hang them at eye level (roughly 145–150 cm to the centre of each print) so the scene reads naturally as you walk past. Because the artwork carries so much white space within it, it works particularly well on white, off-white, or warm stone-toned walls — the prints practically breathe on those backgrounds. If your hallway has a darker wall, the contrast of the black linework against deep charcoal or navy can look absolutely stunning too.

This set suits a Japandi or Japanese-inspired scheme beautifully — think natural wood console tables, woven rattan baskets, and simple ceramic vessels in muted tones. But honestly, it works just as well in a clean Scandi or modern neutral hallway without any other Japanese touches; the restrained palette does all the talking. For more ideas on putting together a calm, considered hallway, have a browse through our Japandi wall art collection — there are some lovely companion pieces in there.

Things Worth Thinking About Before You Choose

The first thing I always consider with a set like this is wall width. These three prints need a decent run of wall to shine — in a narrow hallway, go for smaller individual print sizes so the set fits comfortably without touching door frames or light switches. In a longer corridor, you can go bigger and really let the scene open up. The good news is that the artwork itself is quite vertical in proportion, which is a lovely shape for a hallway wall.

On colour: the art is predominantly black, grey, and white with that one quiet maroon-toned sun at the centre. If your hallway already has warm maroon, burgundy or deep red accents — in a rug, a door, or cushions on a bench — this set will tie in perfectly. If your hallway is cooler and more neutral, the maroon tone just adds a single note of warmth without dominating, which I think is really elegant. Either way, the black linework grounds the whole thing and gives it real presence without being heavy.

Do also think about finish when you select your print type — a Luster paper gives a gentle sheen that makes the blacks really pop, while Museum quality paper has a beautiful flat, gallery-like feel that suits the ink-wash style especially well. Scroll down to see how each size looks in a hallway before you decide.

aiItems.content:
What is calming wall art?

Calming wall art refers to prints, paintings or illustrations designed to bring a sense of peace, stillness and visual quiet to a space — typically through soft or restrained colour palettes, gentle subjects like landscapes or nature scenes, and uncluttered compositions. This set of three Japanese ink-style landscape prints is a great example: the combination of open white space, loose brushwork, black pine silhouettes and a single maroon-toned sun creates an atmosphere of mindful stillness rather than visual noise. Calming wall art is especially popular in hallways, bedrooms and home offices where a sense of relaxation and mental clarity really counts. In Japandi and minimalist interiors, it is often used as the main decorative statement precisely because it does so much with so little.

How to Hang Calming Wall Art in a Hallway

1. Measure your wall first: Hold a piece of tape or use a laser measure to mark out the total width your three prints will occupy, including the gaps between them. Aim for equal spacing — around 5 to 8 cm between each print looks intentional and tidy.

2. Find the right height: The centre of each print should sit at roughly eye level — around 145 to 150 cm from the floor. In a hallway where people walk past rather than sit, slightly higher than a living room is absolutely fine.

3. Start from the centre outward: Mark the centre point of your wall span, position the middle print first, then work outward to the left and right prints. This keeps the set visually balanced even if your hallway is not perfectly symmetrical.

4. Choose your background wall colour thoughtfully: This Japanese ink set works beautifully against white, off-white, warm stone or even deep charcoal walls. The clean white space within the artwork needs room to breathe, so avoid very busy or heavily patterned wallpaper directly behind it.

5. Step back and check before you commit: Use removable adhesive strips or Blu Tack to hold paper templates in position first — it takes five minutes and saves a lot of unnecessary holes in the wall.

Choosing the Right Option for Your Calming Wall Art Prints

Unframed Print — The print is delivered flat and ready for you to frame yourself. Perfect if you already have frames you love or want to match a very specific frame colour to your hallway decor. Available in Luster art paper (gentle sheen, makes blacks really pop) or Museum quality paper (flat, gallery-like surface that suits ink-wash art especially well).

Framed Print — Arrives completely ready to hang straight out of the box — no sourcing frames, no hassle. A brilliant choice if you want a polished, finished look immediately. Also available in Luster or Museum quality paper, so you still get to choose the finish that suits your style.

Wrapped Canvas — The artwork is printed directly onto canvas and stretched over a wooden frame, with the image continuing around the edges for a seamless, contemporary look. No glass, no mount — just the art. Ready to hang and a great fit for a relaxed, modern or Japandi hallway. Available in a range of canvas sizes.

My favourite way to hang this set is in a clean horizontal row at eye level — all three prints evenly spaced above a sofa or a low media console. aiItems.content:
What is a big painting for living room?

A big painting for living room is a large-scale artwork — or a set of prints displayed together — designed to fill and anchor a main living space wall with colour, character and visual impact. In most homes this means a single piece or a coordinated multi-panel set measuring at least 80 cm wide in total, hung above a sofa, fireplace or key furniture piece. Sets of three art prints are one of the most popular formats because they let you cover a wide wall while keeping the artwork light and proportionate. The right big painting brings a room together, sets the mood, and often becomes the first thing guests notice when they walk in.

How to Hang a Big Painting for Living Room: Step-by-Step

1. Measure your wall and furniture: Start by measuring the width of the sofa, console or fireplace the prints will hang above. Aim for your combined print width to be around two-thirds to three-quarters of that furniture width — this gives a balanced, grounded look.

2. Mark the centre point: Find the horizontal centre of your wall or furniture and mark it lightly with a pencil. This is the anchor point for your arrangement.

3. Plan your layout on the floor first: Lay all three prints on the floor in front of you in the order you plan to hang them. Decide on your gap — 5 to 8 cm between each print is ideal for a set like this — and confirm you're happy with the overall spread before you touch the wall.

4. Set your hanging height: The centre of the entire set should sit at roughly eye level — around 145 to 150 cm from the floor is the standard guide. If hanging above a sofa, leave 20 to 25 cm of clear wall between the top of the sofa and the bottom of the lowest print.

5. Mark and hang: Working outward from your centre mark, measure and mark each hanging point. Use a spirit level to keep everything straight, then hang your prints and step back to check the spacing before making any final adjustments.

Choosing Your Format: Unframed, Framed or Wrapped Canvas

Unframed Print — The print is supplied on its own, ready for you to frame yourself. Great if you already have frames you love or want to match an existing set. Available in Luster or Museum quality art paper.

Framed Print — The print arrives ready to hang — no extra trips to the frame shop needed. A brilliant time-saver and the finish looks sharp and considered straight out of the box. Available in Luster or Museum quality art paper.

Wrapped Canvas — Printed directly onto canvas and stretched over a wooden frame, gallery-wrap style. No frame needed and no glass — the image wraps around the sides for a clean, contemporary finish. A great choice if you want a more tactile, studio feel on the wall.

Paper options (prints only) — Luster art paper gives a subtle sheen that makes blacks and contrast really sing. Museum quality paper has a smooth, matte finish that suits the quiet, ink-wash character of this Japanese landscape set particularly well.

aiItems.content:
What is canvas office wall art?

Canvas office wall art refers to decorative art prints or wrapped canvas pieces designed specifically to enhance a workspace — whether that's a home office, a studio or a professional environment. They are printed onto high-quality art paper or canvas and are available unframed, framed or as a wrapped canvas ready to hang. A well-chosen set, like a Japandi Japanese ink-wash landscape, can make an office feel calmer, more focused and far more pleasant to spend time in. Sets of three are particularly popular as they create a cohesive, gallery-style display on a plain office wall without requiring any design expertise to arrange.

How to Hang Canvas Office Wall Art as a Set of 3

1. Measure your wall space: Before you order, measure the width of the wall where you plan to hang the set. Allow a gap of 3–5 cm between each print and a little breathing space on either side of the full group — this keeps the arrangement feeling intentional and balanced rather than cramped.

2. Find your eye level: The centre of the prints should sit roughly at eye level when you're seated at your desk — around 120–130 cm from the floor. This is often lower than people expect, but it makes the art feel part of the room rather than floating above it.

3. Mark lightly with pencil: Use a pencil and a spirit level to mark your hanging points before you put anything on the wall. For a set of three, start with the centre print and work outwards — this is the easiest way to keep the group symmetrical.

4. Hang and step back: Once all three prints are up, step back and check the spacing and level from a distance. Small adjustments are much easier to spot from across the room than up close.

5. Style the space around the art: For a Japandi look, keep the area around the prints clean and uncluttered — a simple desk lamp, a small plant or a neutral storage box is all you need to complete the look.

Choosing the Right Format for Your Canvas Office Wall Art

Format — Unframed Print: The print is delivered rolled or flat, ready for you to frame yourself. Ideal if you already have frames or want to source your own to match your office decor exactly. Available on Luster art paper or Museum quality paper.

Format — Framed Print: Arrives ready to hang straight out of the box — no extra shopping required. The print is mounted and framed for a clean, finished look. Available on Luster art paper or Museum quality paper in multiple sizes.

Format — Wrapped Canvas: The print is stretched over a wooden frame and arrives ready to hang with no additional framing needed. The canvas wrap gives a contemporary, gallery-style finish — particularly effective for bold ink-wash designs like this Japanese landscape set.

Paper finish — Luster: A semi-sheen surface that makes dark tones and fine linework really stand out. Great for high-contrast black and white artwork.

Paper finish — Museum Quality: A flat, fine-art matte finish that closely replicates the look of traditional ink on paper — a natural choice for Japanese and Oriental-style prints like this set.
